title: "Syllabus"
subtitle: "What the four weeks look like"
---

A four-week, ungraded elective, delivered over Zoom, for fourth-year medical
students, running October 12 to November 6, 2026. Nothing in the course needs
an install, a paid account, or a real patient.

## The one idea

**It is your job to learn where AI helps your work.** Nobody can tell you in
advance, and the tools change every few months. You find out by trying, often,
on things that matter to you, and you learn where AI fails the same way. This
course gives you a framework, a routine, and people to try things with. Most of
your learning will be your own, done with AI.

The safety rules are short. **Use your university ChatGPT Edu or Copilot
account. Never put real patient information into a course activity. Check what
matters before you rely on it. You sign the note.** What counts as patient
information is on [its own page](patient-information.qmd).

## Your week

In weeks 2 to 4, the two talks are the main event. The course director
teaches the week's topic live on Monday and a second topic on Wednesday, with
demonstrations on screen. Both are recorded, and watching the recording counts
as attending. The week's core chapter goes with Monday's talk: read it after
the talk, or instead of it if you missed the talk.

Plan on about 8 to 10 hours a week. The table adds up to 7.5 to 9.5 hours for
what is expected, plus anything optional you choose.

| When | What | Expected? | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monday, 10 a.m., 60 minutes, live and recorded | **"How I used AI this week"**: the course director's own real tasks, shown on screen. Then **a talk on the week's core topic**, with live demonstrations | Yes, live or the recording | 1 hour |
| Wednesday, 10 a.m., 60 minutes, live and recorded | **A talk on a second topic**: a menu chapter, or something beyond the book. The class votes on the topic from a short list | Yes, live or the recording | 1 hour |
| After Monday's talk | The week's **core chapter** | Yes | About 1 hour |
| On your own | **[Learn it with AI](learn-with-ai.qmd)**: use AI to teach yourself something you care about. This is the main hands-on work of the course | Yes | 2 to 4 hours |
| Through the week | Guest talks from clinicians and researchers using AI in their work | Attend or watch one | About 1 hour |
| Thursday, 45 minutes, live | **Office hours**: bring what you are stuck on. Not recorded | Optional | 45 minutes |
| Thursday night | [Learning journal](learning-journal.qmd) entry | Yes | 30 minutes |
| Friday, 60 minutes | [Small group](friday-groups.qmd), in one of three time slots you choose: what AI taught you, and practising conversations about AI out loud | Yes, one slot | 1 hour |
| Any time | Chapters from the **menu**, and the [open labs](../appendix/open-labs.qmd) | Optional | As you like |

: Your week, weeks 2 to 4. All times are Mountain time (Denver). Office hours times and the guest schedule are posted in Canvas. {#tbl-week}

## Week 1: live, October 12 to 16

Week 1 is different from the rest. The course director teaches live every
weekday morning, Monday to Thursday, at 10 a.m. Mountain time (Denver). The
small groups meet for the first time on Friday. Canvas has the current
schedule if anything changes.

| Day | Live session |
|---|---|
| Monday, October 12, 10 a.m. | Welcome: how the course works, and how adults learn best |
| Tuesday, October 13, 10 a.m. | A short history of AI |
| Wednesday, October 14, 10 a.m. | What AI is: from AI to machine learning to deep learning to large language models, with time to try it together |
| Thursday, October 15, 10 a.m. | **Hands-on: centaur or cyborg, live.** Everyone in their ChatGPT Edu account at once. Together we try three everyday tasks of a new intern with a chatbot, then decide which to work on with it back and forth and which to hand over and check line by line. Goes with the week's core chapter, [Centaur or cyborg](../chapters/core-centaur-cyborg.qmd). Bring your account; if you cannot sign in yet, come anyway and we will sort it out. |
| Thursday, October 15, after the session | Office hours, by signup. Bring what you are stuck on |
| Friday, October 16 | Small groups, in the time slot you signed up for: introductions, then the first scenario cards |

: Week 1. All times are Mountain time (Denver). {#tbl-week1}

Thursday's session gives you something to write about: your first
[journal entry](learning-journal.qmd) is due that night.

## Weeks 2 to 4: the talks

This is a starting plan, and topics may change. Canvas has the current one.
Each Wednesday topic is chosen by a class vote from the short list below. The
vote runs the week before, so the talk can be prepared. [VERIFY: link to the
vote (a Canvas survey or a Microsoft Form)]{.verify}

**Week 2, October 19 to 23: getting good at it**

- Monday: **Getting good answers.** How a chatbot reads your prompt, with a
  live demonstration. Goes with the core chapter, the
  [prompting lab](../chapters/enrichment-prompting-lab.qmd).
- Wednesday, the class chooses one: **AI for scholarly writing**, or
  **answers that come from real sources** (goes with
  [Grounding AI in real sources](../chapters/enrichment-rag-notebooklm.qmd)).

**Week 3, October 26 to 30: AI and your patients**

- Monday: **Talking with patients about AI**, starting from what patients
  already do with it. Goes with the core chapter,
  [Talking to patients about AI](../chapters/core-patient-communication.qmd).
- Wednesday, the class chooses one: **bias and equity** (goes with
  [Bias and equity](../chapters/core-bias-equity.qmd)), or **building a small
  tool live** (goes with [Agentic coding](../chapters/enrichment-agentic-coding.qmd)).

**Week 4, November 2 to 6: responsibility**

- Monday: **Who answers for the note.** Goes with the core chapter,
  [Ethics, liability, and the device line](../chapters/core-ethics-regulation.qmd).
- Wednesday, no vote: **Where this is going**, for jobs and for the planet,
  and what you will keep from the course. Goes with
  [Will AI take your job?](../chapters/enrichment-workforce-economics.qmd) and
  [What AI costs the planet](../chapters/enrichment-environment.qmd).

## Core and menu, week by week

Each chapter stands alone. The core chapter is the one framework idea for the
week. The menu is there so you can follow what interests you.

| Week | Core | Menu (choose one or more) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 · October 12 to 16 | [Centaur or cyborg](../chapters/core-centaur-cyborg.qmd): what to hand to AI, and what to keep | [How these systems work](../chapters/core-foundations.qmd) (the live talks cover it) |
| 2 · October 19 to 23 | [Prompting lab](../chapters/enrichment-prompting-lab.qmd): getting good answers, and knowing their limits | [Critical appraisal](../chapters/core-appraisal.qmd), [Bias and equity](../chapters/core-bias-equity.qmd), [Grounding AI in real sources](../chapters/enrichment-rag-notebooklm.qmd) |
| 3 · October 26 to 30 | [Talking to patients about AI](../chapters/core-patient-communication.qmd) | [Agentic coding](../chapters/enrichment-agentic-coding.qmd), the [scribe open lab](../appendix/open-labs.qmd) |
| 4 · November 2 to 6 | [Ethics, liability, and the device line](../chapters/core-ethics-regulation.qmd) | [Will AI take your job?](../chapters/enrichment-workforce-economics.qmd), [What AI costs the planet](../chapters/enrichment-environment.qmd) |

: Core chapter and menu. {#tbl-order}

If you are away interviewing, the recordings and the chapters let you keep up.
Watching a talk's recording counts as attending it. Tell the course director
which Friday you will miss, and add one line to that week's journal about a
recording you watched.

## Grading

The course is ungraded. The learning journal is marked complete or incomplete,
with a one-line reply in weeks 1 and 2. What goes in each entry is on the
[learning journal](learning-journal.qmd) page.
